segments.spokenText: Welcome to Project 42. Today we're not just discussing multi-agent theory—we're going to build, stress-test, and watch an agent loop in action.
segments.stageDirection: Instructor avatar fades in on left; hero architecture diagram displays on the right.

visual.description: Clean dark-mode classroom interface displaying learning objectives and the multi-agent topology canvas.
visual.altText: Visual overview of class objectives: agent topologies, memory isolation, and failure recovery.
visual.reducedMotionDescription: Static slide listing the three class objectives.

segments.spokenText: Notice what happens when an autonomous agent makes a tool call. It doesn't execute code directly—it emits a structured JSON payload requesting execution. Let's look at the data flow.
segments.stageDirection: Highlight the request-response boundary on the architecture diagram.

visual.description: Animated diagram highlighting prompt tokenization, tool schema matching, and JSON payload generation.
visual.altText: Diagram showing input tokens entering the model and a structured tool call object being generated.
visual.reducedMotionDescription: Static architecture diagram with highlighted tool-calling boundary.

segments.spokenText: Watch what happens on screen when we send an ambiguous query. The supervisor agent intercepts the prompt, evaluates the required tools, and delegates the task to the researcher subagent.
segments.stageDirection: Live code editor and interactive terminal simulator animate. Highlight lines 14-28 in the code editor, then simulate terminal log output showing step 1 execution.

visual.description: Live IDE simulation: TypeScript code editor on top with synced line highlighting, terminal output panel scrolling below showing structured JSON logs.
visual.altText: Interactive demonstration showing line-by-line execution of a TypeScript supervisor agent and live console logs.
visual.reducedMotionDescription: Static code comparison showing the supervisor delegating to the researcher subagent with terminal output snapshot.

segments.spokenText: Now it's your turn. I've opened the hands-on lab on your right. Implement the circuit breaker threshold to cap iterations at 5 steps, then run the test script.
segments.stageDirection: Instructor gestures toward the interactive lab panel. Class playback pauses until learner submits attempt.
segments.expectedLearnerAction: Configure circuit breaker threshold and execute npm run test:inject-failures in the web sandbox.

segments.spokenText: Let's check your understanding before we move to failure recovery.

feedback.correct: Excellent work. You correctly identified that circuit breakers protect against runaway loops and spend spikes.
feedback.retry: Not quite. Remember that circuit breakers limit step execution rather than expanding context windows. Let's review.

segments.spokenText: You've successfully built and bounded your first multi-agent workflow. Next, we will explore state reconciliation and human-in-the-loop escalation.
segments.stageDirection: Class completion badge animates onto screen.
